en: Theravāda Vinayapiṭaka Mahāvagga 7.
Kathinakkhandhaka (The Chapter on the Kathina)
1. The Authorization of the Kathina.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, there were about thirty bhikkhus from Pāvā, all of whom were forest-dwellers and all of whom were alms-collectors.
All those who were wearers of rag-robes and all those who possessed only three robes, while coming to Sāvatthī to see the Blessed One,
were unable to enter the rains retreat at Sāvatthī as the time for the commencement of the rains approached;
they entered the rains retreat on the way at Sāketa.
They spent the rains residence in a state of longing, thinking: "The Blessed One is staying quite near us, only six yojanas away, yet we do not obtain the opportunity to see the Blessed One.

Then, when those bhikkhus had completed the rains residence, at the end of the three months, after the invitation ceremony (*pavāraṇā*) had been performed, while the rain was falling, they were weary, their robes drenched by the standing water and the mud, and their bodies soaked through.
They went to Sāvatthī, to Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery, where the Blessed One was staying. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side.
Now it is the custom for the Blessed Buddhas to exchange greetings with visiting monks.
Then the Blessed One said this to those monks:
“I hope, monks, that you are enduring; I hope you are getting by;
I hope you have spent the rains residence in comfort, being united, harmonious, and without dispute, and that you did not suffer from lack of almsfood?
“It is endurable, Blessed One; it is getting by, Blessed One.”
“Venerable sir, we have spent the rains residence together in harmony, in mutual agreement, and without dispute, and we have not been troubled for lack of almsfood.
However, venerable sir, while we— some thirty bhikkhus from Pāvā— were on our way to Sāvatthī to see the Blessed One,
as the time for entering the rains residence drew near, we were unable to enter the rains residence at Sāvatthī.”
On the way, we entered the rains retreat at Sāketa.
During that rainy season, venerable sir, we dwelt in a state of longing, thinking:
"The Blessed One is staying nearby, within six yojanas of here, yet we do not obtain the opportunity to see the Blessed One."

“Then, venerable sir, having completed the rains residence and the invitation ceremony at the end of the three months, we have come along the road while it was raining, our robes soaked through by the water and mud and ourselves looking exhausted.
Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this context, gave a discourse on the Dhamma and addressed the bhikkhus:
“I allow you, bhikkhus, for bhikkhus who have completed the rains residence, to spread the kaṭhina.”
“Bhikkhus, for those who have laid aside the kaṭhina, five things will be permissible:

wandering without having been invited, wandering without having taken up the robes, eating in a group, possessing as much robe-cloth as one requires, and whatever robe-material arises there shall belong to them.
Bhikkhus, these five things will be permissible for those who have laid aside the kaṭhina.”
And furthermore, monks, the kaṭhina should be spread in this way:
A learned and competent monk should inform the Saṅgha:
“Let the venerable Saṅgha listen to me.
This cloth for the Kathina has arisen for the Saṅgha.
If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha give this cloth for the Kathina to the monk named so-and-so, in order to spread the Kathina.
This is the motion.
"Venerable sirs, let the Sangha hear me.
This cloth for the Kathina has arisen for the Sangha.
The Sangha gives this cloth for the Kathina to the monk named so-and-so, in order to spread the Kathina."
Whichever venerable one approves of this gift of cloth for the Kathina ceremony being given to the monk named so-and-so in order to spread the Kathina, let him be silent;
whoever does not approve, let him speak.
This cloth for the Kathina ceremony has been given by the Saṅgha to the monk named so-and-so in order to spread the Kathina.
‘The Saṅgha approves; therefore it is silent. Thus do I understand this.
In this way, monks, the kaṭhina is spread; in this way it is not spread.
And how, monks, is the kaṭhina not spread?
The kaṭhina is not considered formally spread merely by marking it out;
the kaṭhina is not considered formally spread merely by washing it;
the kaṭhina is not considered formally spread merely by distributing the robe-cloth.
The kaṭhina is not considered spread merely by cutting;
it is not considered spread merely by sewing; it is not considered spread merely by making the border-fasteners.
The kaṭhina is not considered properly spread merely by the making of the needlework,
nor is it considered properly spread merely by the making of the strengthening work,
nor is it considered properly spread merely by the making of the border.
The kaṭhina is not considered formally spread merely by the making of a border,
nor is it considered formally spread merely by the making of a patch,
nor is it considered formally spread merely by the softening of the wool.
The kaṭhina is not considered properly spread if it is done by means of a sign,
nor is it considered properly spread if it is done by means of indirect talk,
nor is it considered properly spread if it is done in a fraudulent manner.
The kaṭhina is not considered spread by means of what has been stored away;
the kaṭhina is not considered spread by means of what has been relinquished;
the kaṭhina is not considered spread by means of what has not been made allowable.
The kaṭhina is not considered spread except by means of the outer robe;
the kaṭhina is not considered spread except by means of the upper robe;
the kaṭhina is not considered spread except by means of the inner robe.
The kaṭhina is not considered properly spread unless it is made with five robes or more than five, all cut and hemmed on that very day;
nor is the kaṭhina considered properly spread unless it is spread by an individual.
Even if the kaṭhina is properly spread, if one expresses approval while standing outside the boundary, the kaṭhina is likewise considered not properly spread.
In this way, monks, the kaṭhina is not spread.
And how, monks, is the kaṭhina properly spread?
The kaṭhina is properly spread with new cloth, it is properly spread with cloth that is as good as new, it is properly spread with rags.
The kaṭhina is spread; the kaṭhina is spread with rags from a dust heap; the kaṭhina is spread with shop-remnants; the kaṭhina is spread with what is not marked out;
the kaṭhina is spread with what is not formally announced; the kaṭhina is spread with what is not cut up;
the kaṭhina is spread with what is not stored; the kaṭhina is spread with what is not to be relinquished.
The kaṭhina exists; the kaṭhina is spread by means of what has been made allowable; the kaṭhina is spread by means of an outer robe (saṅghāṭī);
the kaṭhina is spread by means of an upper robe (uttarāsaṅga); the kaṭhina is spread by means of a lower robe (antaravāsaka);
or the kaṭhina is spread by means of five or more than five pieces that have been cut and made into circles on that very day.
The kaṭhina is spread for an individual when it has been properly spread.
If the kaṭhina has been properly spread and one standing within the boundary expresses appreciation, then in this way too the kaṭhina is spread.
In this manner, monks, the kaṭhina is spread.
"And how, monks, is the kaṭhina suspended?
There are these eight grounds for the suspension of the kaṭhina:
the end of departure, the end of completion, the end of determination, the end of loss, the end of hearing, the end of hope, the end of crossing the boundary, and simultaneous suspension."
2. The Seven on Taking:
A monk who has finished the robe-making ceremony and has made up his robes takes them and departs, thinking, “I will not return.
For that monk, the suspension of the *kathina* occurs at the moment of departure.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony takes his robe and departs.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: "I shall have this robe made right here; I will not return.
He then has that robe made.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon his final decision.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the spreading of the kaṭhina takes his robe and departs.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I will neither have this robe made up, nor will I return.”
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs by way of formal determination.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina takes his robe and departs.
Once he has gone outside the boundary, it occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here; I will not return.”
He has that robe made. While that robe is being made, it is lost.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs due to loss.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina takes his robe and departs, thinking, “I will return.”
Thus, having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe made.
When the robe is finished, he hears: "It is said that the kaṭhina has been suspended in that residence.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs at the moment of hearing.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony takes his robe and departs, thinking, "I will return.
Having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe made.
Once the robe is finished, thinking, "I will return, I will return," he spends the period beyond the lifting of the Kathina outside [the boundary].
For that bhikkhu, there is the suspension of the kaṭhina by crossing the boundary.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the spreading of the kaṭhina takes his robe and departs, thinking, “I will return.
Having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe made.
Thus, having finished his robe-making, thinking “I shall return, I shall return,” he manages to reach the end of the robe season.
For that bhikkhu, the robe season ends together with the other bhikkhus.
The section on the seven cases involving taking [the robe] is finished.
3. The Group of Seven on Undertaking:
A monk, having undertaken [the robe-making] and having finished making the robe, departs while taking it with him, thinking, "I will not return.
For that monk, the suspension of the *kathina* occurs at the moment of departure.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony takes his robe and departs.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here; I will not return.
He then has that robe made.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon his final decision.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina takes a robe and departs.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I will neither have this robe made up, nor will I return.”
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs by way of his formal decision.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina takes a robe-cloth and departs.
Once he has gone outside the boundary, it occurs to him: “I will have this robe-cloth made right here; I will not return.”
He has that robe made. While that robe is being made, it is lost.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs due to loss.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina takes a robe and departs, thinking, “I will return.”
Thus, having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe made.
When the robe is finished, he hears: “It is said that the kaṭhina has been suspended in that residence.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs at the moment of hearing.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony takes his robe and departs, thinking, “I will return.
Having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe made.
Once the robe is finished, thinking, “I will return, I will return,” he spends time outside the period for the removal of the Kathina.
For that bhikkhu, the kaṭhina is suspended by crossing the boundary.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina takes his robe and departs, thinking, “I will return.
Having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe made.
Thus, having obtained robes, even though he thinks, “I will return, I will return,” he manages to reach the end of the robe season (the *kathina* suspension).
For that bhikkhu, the *kathina* suspension occurs together with the other bhikkhus.
The section on the seven cases involving undertaking is finished.
4. The Group of Six on Taking Up:
A bhikkhu who has participated in the kathina ceremony takes up an unfinished robe and departs.
Once he has gone outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here; I will not return.”
He has that robe made.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon completion [of the robe].
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina departs taking an unfinished robe with him.
When he has gone outside the boundary, it occurs to him: “I will neither have this robe made up nor will I return.
For that monk, the suspension of the kaṭhina is determined by his resolve.
A monk who has spread the kaṭhina departs taking an unfinished robe with him.
While he has gone outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here; I will not return.
He has that robe made. While that robe is being made, it is lost.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon loss.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina takes an unfinished robe and departs, thinking, "I will return.
Having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe made.
When one whose robe has been finished hears:
"The kaṭhina has indeed been suspended in that residence," for that bhikkhu,
the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs at the moment of hearing.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony departs taking with him an unfinished robe-cloth, thinking, "I will return.
Having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe-cloth made up.
Once the robe is finished, thinking, "I will return, I will return," he passes the time outside the boundary until the Kathina suspension occurs.
For that bhikkhu, there is the suspension of the kaṭhina by crossing the boundary.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the spreading of the kaṭhina takes an unfinished robe and departs, thinking, "I will return.
Having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe made.
Thus, one who has finished making robes and thinks, "I shall return, I shall return," achieves the suspension of the *kathina*.
That monk's *kathina* is suspended together with the monks.
The section on "taking up" (ādāya) in groups of six is finished.
5. The Group of Six on Taking Up [the Cloth]:
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony departs taking an unfinished robe-cloth with him.
While he has gone outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe-cloth made right here; I will not return.”
He has that robe made.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon completion.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina departs taking with him an unfinished robe.
When he has gone outside the boundary, it occurs to him: “I will neither have this robe made up nor will I return.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina is determined by his resolve.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the spreading of the kaṭhina departs taking with him an unfinished robe.
While he has gone outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here; I will not return.
He has that robe made. While that robe is being made, it is lost.
For that bhikkhu, there is the suspension of the kaṭhina due to loss.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony departs, taking with him an unfinished robe-cloth, thinking, "I will return.
Having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe-cloth made up.
Once the robe is finished, he hears: "It is said that the Kathina has been suspended in that residence."
For that bhikkhu, the kathina is suspended by hearing [of the robe being made].
A bhikkhu who has spread the kathina departs, taking with him an unfinished robe, thinking, "I will return.
Having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe made.
Thus, having finished his robe-making, he spends time outside the *kaṭhina* period thinking, "I will return, I will return.
For that monk, the *kaṭhina* suspension occurs by crossing the boundary.
A monk who has spread the *kaṭhina* takes up an unfinished robe and departs, thinking, "I will return."
Thus, having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe made.
When the robe is finished, thinking, "I shall return, I shall return," he reaches the time for the suspension of the *kaṭhina*.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the *kaṭhina* occurs together with the other bhikkhus.
The group of six on undertaking is finished.
6. The Group of Fifteen on Taking:
A monk, having laid aside the kaṭhina, departs taking his robe with him.
When he has gone outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here;
I will not return. He has that robe made.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs at the moment of completion.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony takes his robe and departs.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I will neither have this robe made up nor will I return.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the Kathina occurs by way of formal determination.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony takes his robe and departs.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here; I will not return.
He has that robe made, but while it is being made, it is lost.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon loss. [End of] the triad.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina takes a robe and departs, thinking, "I will not return."
When he has gone outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here.
He has that robe made.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs at the moment of completion.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony takes his robe and departs, thinking, "I will not return.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: "I will not have this robe made up.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the Kathina occurs by way of his definitive decision.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony takes his robe and departs, thinking, "I will not return.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him, "I shall have this robe made right here.
He has that robe made. While that robe is being made, it is lost.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon loss. [End of] the triad.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina departs taking a robe-cloth with him, without having determined it; he neither thinks, "I will return," nor does he think, "I will not return."
When he has gone outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here;
I will not return. He has that robe made.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs at the point of completion.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony takes his robe and departs without having determined it. He neither thinks, "I will return," nor does he think, "I will not return.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: "I will neither have this robe made up, nor will I return.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the Kathina occurs through his definitive decision.

A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony takes his robe and departs without having formally determined it as his own. He neither thinks, "I will return," nor does he think, "I will not return.
Having gone outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: "I shall have this robe made right here;
I will not return. He has that robe made. While that robe is being made, it is lost.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon loss. [End of] the triad.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina takes his robe and departs, thinking, "I will return."
While he has gone outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here;
I will not return. He has that robe made.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs at the moment of completion.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony takes his robe and departs, thinking, "I will return.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: "I will neither have this robe made up nor will I return.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the Kathina occurs through his definitive resolve.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony takes his robe and departs, thinking, “I will return.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here; I will not return.
He has that robe made. While that robe is being made, it is lost.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon loss.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina takes his robe and departs, thinking, "I will return.
Having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe made.
Then, having finished making his robe, that bhikkhu hears: “It is said that the kaṭhina has been suspended in that residence.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon hearing it.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina takes his robe and departs, thinking, “I will return.”
Thus, having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe made.
Once the robe is finished, thinking, "I will return, I will return," he passes the time beyond the removal of the kaṭhina outside [the boundary].
For that bhikkhu, there is the removal of the kaṭhina by crossing the boundary.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony takes his robe and departs, thinking, "I will return.
Having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe made.
Once the robe is finished, he thinks, "I will return, I will return," and thus he manages to reach the time for the removal of the Kathina.
The robe-making ceremony (kaṭhina) is suspended for that bhikkhu together with the other bhikkhus.
This concludes the group of six. This concludes the group of fifteen on "taking up" (ādāya).
7. The group of fifteen on "undertaking" (samādāya), etc.

A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony departs taking his robe with him … [to be expanded in detail in the same manner as the section on "taking it"] … A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony departs taking an unfinished robe.
When he has gone outside the boundary, it occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here;
I will not return. He has that robe made.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs at the completion [of the robe]. …pe…
(To be expanded in detail exactly like the *Samādāyavāra*.
8. The Group of Fifteen on Departing with an Incomplete Robe Taken Up:
A monk who has participated in the Kathina ceremony departs after taking up an incomplete robe.
When he has gone outside the boundary, it occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here;
I will not return. He has that robe made.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina is determined by the completion [of the robe].
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony departs, taking with him robe-cloth that has not yet been made up.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I will neither have this robe-cloth made up nor will I return.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the Kathina occurs by means of his definitive resolution.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the robe-making ceremony (atthatakathina) takes up an unfinished robe and departs.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here; I will not return.
He has that robe made, but while it is being made, it is lost.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon loss [of the robe-material]. This concludes the triad.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina departs, taking with him robe-material that is unfinished, thinking, "I will not return."
When he has gone outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here.
He has that robe made.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina is determined by the completion [of the robe].
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony departs, taking with him robe-cloth that has not yet been made up, thinking, "I will not return.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him, "I will not have this robe-cloth made up.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the Kathina occurs by way of his definitive resolve.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony departs taking an unfinished robe-cloth with him, thinking, "I will not return.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him, "I shall have this robe-cloth made right here.
He has that robe-cloth made. While that robe-cloth is being made, it is lost.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon loss. [End of] the triad.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina departs taking an unfinished robe-cloth without having determined it; he neither thinks, “I will return,” nor does he think, “I will not return.”
While he has gone outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here;
I will not return. He has that robe made.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs at the moment of completion.

A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony departs taking an unfinished robe-cloth with him, without having determined it [as his own]. He neither thinks, “I will return,” nor does he think, “I will not return.
When he has gone outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I will neither have this robe-cloth made up, nor will I return.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the Kathina occurs by way of his definitive decision.

A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony departs taking an unfinished robe, without having determined it [as his own]. He does not think, “I will return,” nor does he think, “I will not return.
When he has gone outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here;
I will not return. He has that robe made. While that robe is being made, it is lost.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon loss. [End of] the triad.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina departs taking with him an unfinished robe-cloth, thinking, "I will return."
While he has gone outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: “I shall have this robe made right here;
I will not return. He has that robe made.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs at the moment of completion.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony departs taking an unfinished robe-cloth, thinking, "I will return.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: "I will neither have this robe-cloth made up nor will I return.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the Kathina occurs by way of his definitive resolve.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the kathina ceremony departs taking an unfinished robe-cloth, thinking, "I will return.
While he is outside the boundary, the thought occurs to him: "I shall have this robe-cloth made right here; I will not return.
He has that robe-cloth made. While that robe-cloth is being made, it is lost.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon loss.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina departs taking an unfinished robe-cloth with him, thinking, "I will return.
Having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe-cloth made.
Then a monk whose robe has been finished hears: “It is said that the kaṭhina has been suspended in that residence.
For that monk, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon hearing.
A monk for whom the kaṭhina has been spread takes up an unfinished robe and departs, thinking, “I will return.”
Thus, having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe made.
When the robe is finished, thinking, “I will return, I will return,” he lets the *kaṭhina* suspension pass outside [the boundary].
For that monk, the *kaṭhina* suspension occurs by crossing the boundary.
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony departs taking an unfinished robe-cloth, thinking, "I will return.
Having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe-cloth made.
Once the robe-cloth is finished, he thinks, "I will return, I will return," and thus succeeds in effecting the suspension of the Kathina.
The robe-making ceremony (kaṭhina) is suspended for that bhikkhu together with the other bhikkhus.
This concludes the group of six. This concludes the section of fifteen items concerning undertaking.
This concludes the recitation chapter concerning taking up.
9. The Group of Twelve on Non-Seeking:
A bhikkhu who has participated in the Kathina ceremony departs with the expectation of obtaining robe-cloth.
Having gone outside the boundary, he waits for that expectation of robe-cloth.
One gains it without expectation; one does not gain it through expectation.
It occurs to him: "I shall have this robe made right here; I will not return. He has that robe made.
For that bhikkhu, the suspension of the kaṭhina occurs upon his reaching a decision.
A bhikkhu who has spread the kaṭhina departs with the expectation of obtaining a robe.
Having gone outside the boundary, he attends to that expectation for a robe.

14. Discourse on Obstacles and Non-Obstacles:
"Monks, there are these two obstacles to the *kaṭhina* and two non-obstacles.
And what, monks, are the two obstacles to the *kaṭhina*?"
The impediment of the dwelling and the impediment of the robes.
And how, monks, is there the impediment of the dwelling?
Here, monks, a monk either dwells in that dwelling or departs from it with longing, thinking, "I shall return."
In this way, monks, there is the impediment of the dwelling place.
And how, monks, is there the impediment of robes?
Here, monks, a monk’s robe is either unfinished or half-finished, or his expectation of obtaining a robe has not been cut off.
In this way, monks, there is the obstacle of robes.
These, monks, are the two obstacles to the kaṭhina.
And what, monks, are the two non-obstacles to the kaṭhina?
The impediment of the dwelling and the impediment of the robe.
And how, monks, is there the impediment of the dwelling?
Here, monks, a monk departs from that dwelling, having cast it off, vomited it out, released it, and being without regard for it, thinking, "I shall not return."
In this way, monks, there is no impediment regarding the dwelling place.
And how, monks, is there no impediment regarding robes?
Here, monks, a monk’s robe has been finished, or it has been lost, or ruined, or burnt, or his expectation for a robe has ceased.
“In this way, monks, there is no obstacle regarding robes.
These, monks, are the two obstacles to the *kathina* [privileges].
The seventh chapter on the *Kathina* is finished.

One standing within the boundary gives thanks.
Thus is the exposition of the spreading of the kaṭhina,
consisting of eight summary headings regarding its suspension.
Departure means completion,
as well as final determination and removal.
Hearing means the cutting off of hope.
The eighth [offense] is for exceeding the boundary;
taking the robe that has been made,
one goes away with the thought, "I will not return."
For him, that lifting of the kaṭhina occurs by way of departure;
he goes away taking his robe with him.
Outside the boundary, he thought this:
"I will have it made, but I shall not return.
Upon its completion, there is the suspension of the *kaṭhina*.
Having taken [the kaṭhina] outside the boundary,
with the thought "I shall not return," his kaṭhinuddhāra occurs.
One who is bound by the determination [to finish the robe] may go taking the robe with him;
having gone outside the boundary, he reflects thus:
“‘I will perform [the duty], I will not return’—
while he is doing it, it is lost;
for him, that is the lifting of the *kaṭhina*.”
It does not end with non-existence.
Having taken it, he goes thinking,
"I will return," and he has the robe made outside.
If a monk who possesses a robe hears that the kaṭhina has been removed there, for him that is the removal of the kaṭhina.
He becomes one who ends the observance day;
taking [the robe] with him, he departs thinking, "I will return," and has the robe made outside [the monastery].
If the robe-material is outside,
it effects the suspension of the kaṭhina;
for him, that is the suspension of the kaṭhina.
One who goes beyond the boundary:
having taken [the robe] and going away with the intention "I will return," one has the robe made outside [the boundary].
"I shall go back for my robe-cloth;
the suspension of the *kathina* is now complete. For him, that suspension of the *kathina* [is valid].
Together with the monks it arises;
taking up and fully undertaking,
there are sevenfold and sevenfold destinies.
There is no [offense] upon departing;
when the group of six has dispersed, there is a destination;
having taken [the robe], one who has gone beyond the boundary [is at fault].
"I shall cause it to be done"—thus [the thought] arises.
Completion, determination, and removal:
these are the three.
"Having taken it, thinking 'I will not return,' [and] 'I shall do it outside the boundary'—
this is completion as well as formal determination."
This [method] does not apply even to non-existence;
for one who has not made a resolution, it is not so—
thus there are three below, according to the method of the system.
"Having taken it, he goes away,
thinking, 'I will return and place it outside the boundary'; yet he makes it so that he does not return."
The suspension of the kaṭhina occurs through completion,
through formal determination, through departure,
and by crossing the boundary of hearing.
Together with the monks, let this fifteenth destination arise:
those who have undertaken [the path] but left it unfinished.
And likewise, having undertaken them again;
these are your four turns,
all of which consist of fifteen methods.
The desireless, the desiring,
and that which is to be done— these three you should understand by way of their guidance.
Three [groups], twelve, and twelve.
Herein, there are nine apavilāna states,
and therein five kinds of comfort.
The summary of obstacles and non-obstacles has been made according to its method.
In this Khandhaka, there are one hundred and eighteen bases consisting of twelve repetitions of the formula.
The Chapter on the Kathina is finished.
